title: Squeezing-type lower bounds on generalized metrological sensitivity
abstract: We introduce squeezing-type lower bounds for a hierarchy of variance bounds under specific unbiasedness constraints, which generalizes the quantum Cramér-Rao bound. Our construction directly extends standard squeezing coefficients to the corresponding generalized metrological sensitivities while retaining their experimentally accessible structure. We show how observables maximizing these bounds can be identified analytically within families of accessible observables. If arbitrary observables are accessible, the optimized squeezing-type bound recovers the exact generalized metrological sensitivity. These bounds provide efficient and experimentally viable characterizations of generalized metrological sensitivities that are especially relevant in finite-shot scenarios and in the transition from local to global parameter estimation.
summary: This paper introduces generalized squeezing-type lower bounds that extend the standard Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound to a hierarchy of metrological sensitivities. By analyzing moment-based and test-observable constructions, the authors provide theoretically rigorous and experimentally accessible ways to characterize quantum estimation limits. This is vital for designing high-precision quantum sensors in both theoretical and physical systems.
main_problem: The paper develops and characterizes squeezing-type lower bounds for a hierarchy of generalized metrological sensitivities, aiming to generalize the standard Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound.
main_result: The authors introduce squeezing-type bounds that provide efficient and experimentally viable characterizations of generalized metrological sensitivities, recovering the exact sensitivity when arbitrary observables are accessible.
method: The methodology involves constructing generalized bounds using test observables and associated bias constraints, leading to quantum information matrices ($\mathbf{Q}$) and deriving bounds based on these matrices.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general quantum systems parameterized by a state $ho(	heta)$ and measured via a POVM $\{E_x\}_x$. Specific examples include collective spin systems undergoing One-Axis-Twisting (OAT) dynamics.
key_observables: Metrological sensitivity, Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), generalized squeezing parameters ($\chi_{-2}$), and various information matrices ($\mathbf{C}, \mathbf{Q}$).
important_parameters: The parameter $	heta$ being estimated, the number of qubits $N$, and the noise admixture $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares results derived from the QFI (standard bound) against bounds derived from finite-displacement constructions or moment-based approaches.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares various squeezing sensitivities (HCR and Abel constructions) against the standard QFI, showing how the optimal displacement $\lambda$ shifts over time.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the standard QCRB to a generalized framework involving multiple test observables and bias constraints. It then introduces moment-based and squeezing-type parameters ($\mu_{-2}, \chi_{-2}$) to establish lower bounds on the quantum information function ($	ext{IQ}$). Finally, it applies this framework to specific physical models like OAT dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic theoretical tool to quantify estimation precision beyond the standard QFI, which is crucial for designing optimal quantum sensing protocols in complex, realistic scenarios.
